architecture.summary: GitHub Pages serves static files. Application code on the Pages origin cannot read the visitor IP. A suggestion has to be a browser request to a public HTTPS endpoint. The browser, not Pages, is the client the provider sees. This evaluation sent GET requests with an Origin header from the evaluation host. It did not execute JavaScript on the Pages site and it did not record IP addresses, coordinates, city names, or postal codes.

runtime_policy.attribution: Country data includes GeoLite2 data created by MaxMind, available from https://www.maxmind.com.

selected_evidence.terms_summary: The public page says api.country.is is free, requires no key, and is free for commercial use. It has run since 2015. It tells critical applications to self-host. Self-hosting asks for a MaxMind account id and license key, which this static site will not use.

cors.notes: Both Pages origins received Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on a queryless HTTPS GET. Accept: application/json is a CORS-safelisted request header, so the browser does not need a preflight. The client sends credentials omit, mode cors, redirect error, cache no-store, and referrerPolicy no-referrer so a search string in the page URL is not attached as a Referer. Hash routes already keep the search fragment off the Referer.

quota.summary: The public page says there is no quota and the infrastructure rate-limits to 10 requests per second per IP to prevent abuse. The client allows one request per browser session and does not retry.

precision.summary: GET / with no query returns an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code and an IP field. The published optional fields parameter can add city, subdivision, postal code, coordinates, and ASN. This client does not send fields. The kept result is the country code only. A VPN, mobile carrier, or anycast address can make the country wrong. The code is not a place id and it does not select a city. Data is MaxMind GeoLite2, updated daily, with Cloudflare geolocation when that source is available.

retention.provider_summary: The public page answers “Do you log requests?” with “No.” The response body still contains an IP field. The client drops that field and does not write it, or any coordinates, into localStorage or sessionStorage. The opt-out record stores only the schema and optedOut true. The session record stores only the schema and a request count of 1.

known_limits: Provider terms can change after 2026-10-30. This record is the check that selected the current endpoint.
The CORS probe used an Origin header from the evaluation host. It was not a browser running on GitHub Pages.
The selected response includes an IP field. The client discards it and does not store it.
A country code is not a stable place id. With no resolver, the place stays unselected and manual search stays complete.
A resolver may map the country code to a stable country place id. It cannot map that code to a city.
The default does not ask for consent before the single request. A deployment can set consentRequired and the client then waits for Suggest my approximate location.
This record is not a legal opinion that disclosure satisfies every ePrivacy rule.
country.is publishes no SLA. Timeout, HTTP errors, and an unreadable body leave manual search in place.
One failed attempt still consumes the session request so the client does not retry in a loop.
